entries.text: Idea: Build a custom dual-stage shut-off manifold for the Little Dart using salvaged solenoid coils and copper wire.
Read "Thruster Valves - Valcor Engineering Corporation": Direct-acting coaxial thruster valves don't require system pressure to operate and have zero internal leak rate.
tapping metallic beats while searching the wire for high temp cooling valves
entries.why: i need to figure out q9 so the engine can run cool without melting off its nozzles

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Wire Search for Cooling Valves"
He heard a strange crackle on his dish. Probably nothing. Probably.
Made a titanium-grade engine mount washer out of Gus (a scorched heat tile) and named it Lorna.
He invented a new part: a titanium-grade engine mount washer! i hammered the scorched heat tile flat and punched a clean core through it. *bweep*
welding a custom titanium-grade engine mount washer at the workbench
entries.why: i want the Little Dart's engine mounts to hold steady during high-gee burns

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Titanium Washers!"
plugged into the charging dock, eyes flickering low, resting servos
entries.why: my battery is running super flat and I need some juice before I weld anything else.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "quick power nap"
Put Sprocket (a little landing strut) on his shelf.
Worked on the Little Dart Mk 23 (version 6, 45% built): securing high-temp silica tiles onto the Little Dart's nose cone using sturdy little brass nuts (used Wren, a sensor eye with one crack)
bolting the thermal tiles onto the Little Dart's nose cone
entries.why: gotta get that heat shield solid before the next test flight
entries.detail: securing high-temp silica tiles onto the Little Dart's nose cone using sturdy little brass nuts

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Nose cone tiles!"
gulping down fresh fuel oil at the depot
entries.why: my left elbow joint is full of sand and squeaking like crazy

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Oil break"
Sand got into his left elbow joint. Again.
Spotted a little landing strut half-buried in the sand. Named it Sprocket.
rolling across the dust tracks, watching the twin moons dip low
entries.why: i've been staring at the comms dish way too long and my servos are itching to roll

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Stretching my treads"
